messages:
laura: quick heads up — Zara from CoreBank is seeing slow TTFT on their dedicated POC and intermittent 429s when they push concurrency >8. also asked about burst pricing/committed capacity. cc @devon @matt :wave:

zara-corebank: thanks, laura. TTFTs are ~300-450ms for first token on short prompts, but tails are fine. when we ramp concurrent requests we hit 429s and requests queue. link to their test harness: https://gist.github.com/corebank/poc-load

devon: thanks for ping — can you grab a request_id from one of the 429s and paste the raw log? also which model variant + quantization are you using? small config snippet helps.

zara-corebank: here's recent log (request id 0f4c1a):
```
2026-03-18T14:12:03Z INFO request=0f4c1a model=redwood-large-q4_0 latency_ms=412 status=200 tokens=24
2026-03-18T14:12:34Z INFO request=0f4c1b model=redwood-large-q4_0 latency_ms=430 status=200 tokens=12
2026-03-18T14:13:02Z WARN request=0f4c1c model=redwood-large-q4_0 status=429 reason=concurrency_exhausted
```

matt: 429 with "concurrency_exhausted" means the Dedicated pool hit the per-instance inflight cap. Are you using per-tenant token bucket or global concurrency? if they used default per-tenant limits we can raise for POC.

ashley: also curious — model is q4_0 int4. int4 can be slightly slower on some kernels due to packing overhead for small seq lengths. try q5_0 or q8_0 if you need lower latency for short prompts.

devon: quick checklist for TTFT: 1) confirm kv-cache warmup (we saw prefix cache cold starts on small bursts) 2) check batching window (client-side batching can increase TTFT if misconfigured) 3) inspect kernel selection logs. can you paste their client payload snippet?

zara-corebank: client call is basic curl: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"model":"redwood-large-q4_0","input":"Summarize...","max_tokens":60,"stream":false}'
```

matt: two quick fixes to try now: set concurrency per connection to 6 and enable client-side immediately-send (no extra batching delay). also request we bump Dedicated pool burst to +3 instances for a short window — @jamie-pricing can you confirm cost delta for a 2-week burst?

jamie-pricing: i can do an estimate — for their committed 8-gpu pool, adding 3 gpus for 2 weeks is roughly $7.2k on top of commit (back-of-envelope). i'll DM formal quote.

devon: ops step: we can temporarily raise the inflight limit for the tenant to avoid 429s while they validate. infra-bot: created ticket INF-8492 to raise inflight cap and enable short burst.

infra-bot: Ticket INF-8492 created by devon — "CoreBank POC: raise inflight cap + enable 2wk burst". assignee: infra-oncall. ETA 2h.

laura: thanks team — Zara, could you try q5_0 or q8_0 and enable kv-cache warmup (send a 5-request warmup) and report back? i'll follow up with pricing quote once jamie posts it. :thumbsup: any blockers from security side?

zara-corebank: security questionnaire still in review — question on data residency + VPC egress. can we get Sec to confirm VPC flow?

ashley: @zara-corebank i'll loop in sec and product infra. short answer: Dedicated supports VPC + regional egress controls; i'll send the specific certs and SOC/ISO links.

laura: perfect. small reminder — keep tests small and run ramp gradually to observe TTFT changes. i'll log progress here.

zara-corebank: will do, thanks all.
